title: Mary Gay Scanlon addresses veterans' treatment and government data use allegations - South Delco News
text:
Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon, who represents Pennsylvania’s 5th district in the U.S. Congress, posted a series of statements on her social media account on December 11, 2025, addressing issues related to veterans and alleged government misuse of personal data.
In her first post at 18:41 UTC, Scanlon wrote, “People who have served our country and put their lives on the line for our rights are NOT the worst of the worst.”
Later that day at 19:00 UTC, she raised concerns about federal data collection practices under the current administration. Scanlon stated, “This administration has mobilized the government to collect Americans’ private Social Security, tax, student loan, health care, voter registration, and SNAP data and then use it in illegal law enforcement activities and prosecutions of the President’s political enemies.”
Shortly after at 19:02 UTC, she added another comment: “You can run, but you can’t hide from accountability. The American people deserve answers.”
Scanlon has served as a member of Congress since 2018 after replacing Pat Meehan. She was born in Watertown, New York in 1959 and currently resides in Swarthmore. Scanlon graduated from Colgate University with a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1980 and earned her Juris Doctor from the University of Pennsylvania in 1984.
